title: Decentralized throttler fabric and degradation policy for fair burst handling
creator: Sasha Mehra
description: Problem: Our current centralized quota coordinator exhibits tail amplification during cross-region network partitions and when the coordinator is under maintenance. Tenants experience long tail latency or opaque 503s during bursts. We need a design that preserves SLOs (p50/p95/p99 for token responses), maintains fairness across tenants during short bursts, and enables graceful degraded behavior when limiter components become unavailable.
background: Recent incidents (postmortem: incident-2026-01-rate-flood) showed: 1) central lease renewal stalls caused global shedding with poor tenant differentiation; 2) temporary partitions led to sudden drops to fail-closed behavior; 3) customers saw unrelated tenants consume burst tokens unfairly. Existing ENG tickets focus on backpressure smoothing and regional circuit breakers, but we lack a cohesive strategy that combines local fast-paths, conservative global coordination, and degradable responses that keep apps online.
goals: 1) Allow per-region/local proxies to service short spikes (burst buffering) without contacting global coordinator for every request. 2) Guarantee fairness across tenants for multi-second bursts and avoid token-starvation. 3) Provide deterministic degraded modes when central quota store is unreachable: soft-degrade (rate-limited best-effort with headers) and hard-degrade (circuit-breaker reject). 4) Keep SLOs intact: p50/p95 latency targets and <1% error budget burn caused by limiter failures.
proposed_solution: Introduce a decentralized throttler fabric: each region runs a local throttler that maintains a conservative local token bucket derived from periodic, inexpensive leases from the global metering service. Leases are opaque, renewable credits that amortize global coordination. Local throttlers serve requests from their local bucket for short bursts (<10s window). For sustained higher throughput, local throttlers consult global metering asynchronously to top up or throttle back.
implementation_details: - Lease format: opaque lease token with (tenant_id, tokens_granted, expiry, generation) signed by global metering service. - Local fast-path: validate lease signature, decrement local counter in shared memory (atomic). No network call for typical token consumption. - Refill strategy: background renewal at 20% remaining threshold; exponential backoff on renewal failures. - Circuit-breaker tiers: green (fully functional), amber (lease renewal failing but local tokens available => soft-degrade), red (local tokens exhausted and cannot renew => hard-degrade/short-circuit). - Fairness mechanism: borrow-smoothing window where local throttlers share periodic delta metrics to the global metering service to rebalance allocations across regions every minute. - Metric tagging: per-tenant, per-region counters for granted/used/denied tokens and lease failures.
tradeoffs: - Pros: reduces coordination latency for bursts, improves p95/p99 during transient spikes, clearer degraded semantics. - Cons: eventual divergence risk (local allocations become stale), additional complexity (lease signing, token sync protocol), extra telemetry and storage costs for delta reconciliation. - We bias safety: leases conservative (under-provision) to avoid overcommit; this may increase rejections under pathological global surge scenarios.
acceptance_criteria: Local fast-path handles 95% of requests during 5s simulated bursts in a single region without global calls
Multi-region fairness: simulated 60/40 traffic split should not allow the smaller tenant to be starved for >30s under burst tests
Degraded modes observable: amber and red states emit structured events and client-facing headers (X-Redwood-Limiter-State)
SLO impact: new throttler must not increase production p95 latency by more than 5% and must keep limiter-induced 5xx under 0.5% after rollout
Failover test: global metering pod restarts with 30s downtime must not cause global outage; local soft-degrade should keep tail errors within budget
test_plan: 1) Unit tests for lease parsing, atomic counters, and signature verification. 2) Integration test harness (locally emulated multi-region) that injects network partitions and measures token consumption, latency and rejection rates. 3) Chaos test: kill global metering pods and validate amber/red transitions and correct events. 4) Load test with realistic tenant mixes (10k tenants with 99th-percentile behavior) using the benchmark suite in infra/benchmarks/quotas.
rollout_plan: Phase 1: Deploy local throttler library behind a feature flag in non-prod regions; collect metrics for 2 weeks. Phase 2: Canary to 10% of production traffic (single region) with auto rollback on SLO regressions. Phase 3: Staged multi-region rollout with global metering compat mode enabled. Phase 4: Flip default to decentralized fabric and deprecate central fast-path after 6 weeks of stable metrics.
monitoring: - Dashboards: per-region token consumption, lease renew success rate, lease lag (time between global allocation and local consumption), amber/red node counts. - Alerts: lease_renew_fail_rate > 3% for 5m, local_denies_rate increase > 2x baseline for 10m, cross-region imbalance signal if one tenant consumes >3x its expected allocation. - SLO dashboards show limiter-induced latency and error impact correlated with feature flag.
